Subject: Initial redline — IP routing, output ownership & feedback license

Team,

Thanks for sending the draft order form redlines. High level concerns from our side:
- Novum's proposed assignment language appears to assign broad "deliverable" IP including model outputs and downstream productization; that's more than we typically accept.
- The feedback/training license ask is open-ended. We can accept a limited feedback license to improve the service (bug fixes, safety, reliability) but not a perpetual productive training right without compensation or opt-out.
- Telemetry/telemetry exports: we need a clear carve (telemetry for ops vs. training).

Attached is a short excerpt with the problematic clauses highlighted (redline_excerpt.docx). Can you confirm the non-negotiables on your side and propose a tractable path (specific clause swaps or a fallback exhibit)?

Suggested next steps: mutual action plan + single call with legal + product. Proposed times: Wed/Thu this week.

Rafael Mendes
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alice Kim <alice.kim@novumcorp.com>

Date: 2026-11-25T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial redline — IP routing, output ownership & feedback license

Hi Rafael,

Appreciate the quick flag. A few points from Novum Legal: we require assignment of customer-facing deliverables that are incorporated into our products (we view this as standard for productization rights). We are willing to limit types of data used for training but not to carve out an expansive telemetry blanket that impedes product improvement.

Specific asks from our side:
1) Assignments for "Customer Deliverables" (defined) with an express carve for underlying model weights/architectural IP retained by vendor.
2) A royalty-free, perpetual license for feedback that allows Novum to productize improvements derived from the deliverables.
3) Operational telemetry may be shared with Redwood only for debugging; training use should be allowed unless we agree on an opt-out and associated fee.

I'll attach our annotated redlines (Novum_redlines.pdf). We're open to a one-hour call to triage and align. If you can send counter-language prior to the call that will help.

Thanks,
Alice Kim
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Novum Corp

1) Laura: propose redline countertext (sample clause) by EOD Friday (48h).

3) Kimberly: confirm operational telemetry gate (what we can share for ops vs. training).

Rafael/Team,

Thanks for the heads up. I reviewed Novum's redlines. We can propose the following compromise path that is defensible and keeps long-term product risk manageable:

1) Customer Deliverables assignment: accept assignment only for materials that are (i) explicitly defined as "Customer Deliverables" in the Order Form (deliverable artifacts exported as static files or components) and (ii) not derived from our internal model weights. Add a definitional exhibit to restrict scope.

2) Feedback license: offer a limited, perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use customer-provided feedback for service improvement and bug fixes (including internal model tuning), but exclude general-purpose model retraining that would be redistributed or sold as a standalone model. If Novum wants productization (sell as a feature outside their org), require additional commercial terms (fee or revenue share). Sample redline attached: proposed_clause.txt.

3) Telemetry: split telemetry into two buckets — "Operational Telemetry" (logs, error traces) for debugging and support; and "Training Data" (content intended to train models). Allow operational telemetry by default; require explicit opt-in plus fee/controls for training use.

I'll add inline markup to their PDF once we agree on the approach. If sales wants a concession path, we can mirror it in the order form: a timebound trial for productization rights (e.g., six months with review).

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
